subsystems.name: Display stack
subsystems.role: draws each eye's image at high resolution and frame rate.
parts: micro-OLED on silicon, or fast LCD with backlight

subsystems.name: Optics
subsystems.role: magnifies a small display into a wide field of view while keeping the headset thin.
parts: pancake lens stack (polariser, partially reflective mirror, quarter-wave plate)
or waveguide combiner for see-through AR

subsystems.name: Tracking sensors
subsystems.role: work out where the head and hands are, without external base stations.

subsystems.name: Passthrough pipeline
subsystems.role: shows the real world on the screens so digital objects appear placed in it.

subsystems.name: Compute and power
subsystems.role: runs the scene, tracking and rendering inside a wearable package.
parts: mobile system-on-chip with GPU and neural accelerator
heat spreader and fan or passive cooling

subsystems.name: Audio and comfort
subsystems.role: makes the device usable for long sessions.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Ray-tracing software picks lens curvatures and coatings so the display thumbnail fills a wide field of view with sharp edges and tolerable distortion.

buildSteps.title: Make the displays
buildSteps.detail: Micro-OLED pixels are deposited on a silicon backplane; each eye needs roughly 2000×2000 pixels or more, refreshed at 90 Hz or faster.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the optics
buildSteps.detail: Precision-moulded polymer lenses are coated with polarising and partially reflective films, then laminated into a folded pancake stack a few centimetres deep.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensor ring
buildSteps.detail: Camera modules, an inertial measurement unit and depth projectors are mounted around the frame, then factory-calibrated against each other.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The system-on-chip, memory, radios and battery are placed on a compact board, with thermal paths to the frame.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and align
buildSteps.detail: Optics, displays and sensors are assembled under clean conditions; each eye's display is aligned to its lens to a small fraction of a degree.

buildSteps.title: Write the runtime
buildSteps.detail: A compositor fuses camera frames, head pose prediction and rendered imagery, aiming to keep motion-to-photon latency under about 20 ms so the view feels stable.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Per-unit calibration corrects lens distortion and colour, then units are drop-tested, sweat-tested and burn-in tested.

prerequisites.why: the image must pack more than about 2000 pixels into each eye over a wide field of view to look sharp.
they fold the light path so a wide field of view fits in a device light enough to wear.
rendering two high-resolution views at 90 Hz must run on battery.
cameras plus an inertial sensor give head and hand pose without external beacons.
they are still dim and narrow compared with opaque headsets, limiting outdoor AR.

pathway.milestone: mixed-reality headsets with colour passthrough, hand tracking and roughly 500 g weight
pathway.unlocks: virtual screens, training, design review and gaming in one device.

pathway.milestone: eye-tracked foveated rendering and varifocal optics
pathway.unlocks: sharper images at lower power and comfortable viewing at close range.

pathway.milestone: slimmer see-through AR glasses with brighter waveguides
pathway.unlocks: all-day wear indoors and outdoors, not just short sessions.

pathway.milestone: offloading heavy rendering to phones, PCs or edge servers over low-latency wireless
pathway.unlocks: glasses-like devices with far less weight and heat.
